plannedSets.$comment: docs/transformation-audit.md §10.3's generation plan, the batch-D slice of it (SET A–F, 28 entries). EVERY ENTRY HAS NOW BEEN GENERATED and its result URLs are recorded in `candidates` — 56 renders, two variants each, made 2026-09-04 through the Higgsfield MCP on the same `model` and `promptSuffix` the built `assets` used. What is NOT done is everything that needs the file itself: `keeper` is still null and `status` is still "planned" for all 28, because the masters cannot be built in a session — the CDN holding these URLs answers 403 to the agent proxy's egress policy, which is an organization policy denial to report, not to route around. Leaving them "planned" is deliberate and load-bearing: `--promote` flips a row to "promoted", and from that moment bundled-media.test.ts demands the master exist ON DISK and media-v3-preflight.mjs demands a culled `keeper`, so promoting a row whose file nobody has downloaded turns the build red. The remaining sequence, on any machine with ordinary internet: `node scripts/media-v3-fetch.mjs --promote <id>` (no URLs needed — it falls back to the candidates recorded here), then `--candidates` to cull and set "keeper", then the default run to write the AVIF master and its LQIP, then point a slot at the file in /studio/site-images, because a built master is not a wired one. SET F rows are loops: build them with media-v3-video-fetch.mjs, not the still pipeline. Their variant `a` was re-generated at 1080p (1920x1080, the entry's targetWidth) with generate_audio false, because the first pass took seedance_2_5's 720p default and its audio-on default — under-spec on width, and audio is wasted bytes against §15.3's 2.5 MB ceiling on a surface HeroMedia plays muted and aria-hidden. The 720p clip is kept as variant `b`, marked offSpec, the way videos[0].candidates[a] records its own short clip. `--planned` prints the queue and that whole sequence. These URLs are not permanent — the previous batch's were re-verified alive eight days after generation, so treat that as the working window and re-generate from the same prompts if they have expired. BATCH E (2026-09-05) adds five more sets — varmala-preservation, gifting, workshops, atelier and studio-chrome, 29 entries — chosen from a slot audit rather than a wish list: the 76 registry slots are backed by only 25 distinct files, `tile-live.avif` alone carries 8 of them and `tile-create.avif` 7, so each entry names the specific over-worked master it is meant to relieve. The maker portrait is deliberately NOT in this queue: §15.2 forbids a generated maker, and a row in a generation queue is an invitation to generate it. It stays what it has always been — the owner's to photograph.

sets.atelier: SET J — the atelier and the brand story, for /about. One room, its tools, its shelves and its cure room. The maker portrait in this set is a BRIEF, never a generation (§15.2).
sets.studio-chrome: SET K — backdrops for the staff Studio's own chrome: the four auth screens and the empty states. Dark, quiet, and composed so a form column can sit over one half without fighting the picture.

notes: 2026-09-05 — batch E shipped 29 entries and two of them were wrong to queue. `varmala-before-after` was a 3:2 restatement of excluded[0]: §15.2 forbids a generated picture standing in for a customer's own flowers, and changing the ratio does not change the claim the picture makes. `varmala-floret-macro` had nowhere to land — the only 1:1 slots are about.material1-4.macro, and §15.3 generated those four as one batch on identical ground and light, so swapping one member for a different set's frame is exactly the incoherence §15.3 exists to prevent. Both are deleted rather than re-prompted. Three placements in the same set were rewritten because they claimed to free or replace a file they do not actually touch.
